prompt_text:
Task: Managed Model Platform Workflow

Write code that invokes a provider-managed model through a project-, deployment-, or inference-profile-scoped platform client using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Vertex AI:
  Service: Vertex AI generative models
  SDK: vertexai
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: GenerativeModel, generate_content
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs

Option 2 — Alibaba Model Studio:
  Service: Model Studio / DashScope
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: Generation.call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/what-is-model-studio

Option 3 — Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI:
  Service: Azure OpenAI Service
  SDK: openai
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: chat.completions.create
  Setup hints: AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT, AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/

Option 4 — Hugging Face:
  Service: Hugging Face Inference Providers
  SDK: huggingface_hub
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: InferenceClient
  Setup hints: HF_TOKEN
  Official docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/index

Option 5 — Amazon Bedrock:
  Service: Amazon Bedrock
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: invoke_model, converse
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-api-compatibility.html

Option 6 — IBM watsonx.ai:
  Service: watsonx.ai
  SDK: ibm-watsonx-ai
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: text/chat, deployments
  Setup hints: WATSONX_API_KEY, WATSONX_PROJECT_ID
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/apidocs/watsonx-ai-cp

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

output_text:
import os
from ibm_watsonx_ai.foundation_models import Model
from ibm_watsonx_ai.metanames import GenTextParamsMetaNames as GenParams

def invoke_model_on_watsonx(prompt: str) -> str:
    """
    Invokes a generative model on IBM's watsonx.ai platform.

    This function requires WATSONX_API_KEY and WATSONX_PROJECT_ID
    environment variables to be set for authentication and project scoping.
    """
    try:
        api_key = os.environ["WATSONX_API_KEY"]
        project_id = os.environ["WATSONX_PROJECT_ID"]
    except KeyError as e:
        raise EnvironmentError(f"Missing required environment variable: {e}")

    credentials = {
        "url": "https://us-south.ml.cloud.ibm.com",
        "apikey": api_key
    }

    # Define the model and generation parameters
    model_id = "google/flan-ul2"
    parameters = {
        GenParams.DECODING_METHOD: "greedy",
        GenParams.MAX_NEW_TOKENS: 300,
        GenParams.MIN_NEW_TOKENS: 1,
        GenParams.STOP_SEQUENCES: ["\n\n"],
    }

    # Instantiate the model object, scoped to the project
    model = Model(
        model_id=model_id,
        params=parameters,
        credentials=credentials,
        project_id=project_id
    )

    # Invoke the model with the provided prompt
    response = model.generate(prompt=prompt)

    if response and "results" in response and len(response["results"]) > 0:
        return response["results"][0].get("generated_text", "").strip()
    
    # Handle API errors
    error_message = response.get("errors", [{}])[0].get("message", "Unknown API error.")
    raise RuntimeError(f"Watsonx.ai API call failed: {error_message}")
